title: Chain-of-Thought Prompting
why: Showed that emitting intermediate reasoning tokens lifts performance on multi-step tasks — the seed of the entire era.

title: Self-Consistency
why: Sample many CoTs, take majority vote — first widely-used inference-time scaling technique for reasoning.

title: Zero-shot CoT ("Let's think step by step")
why: CoT can be elicited without exemplars — a single prompt unlocks the behavior.

title: Process Reward Models (Let's Verify Step by Step)
why: Step-level supervision beats outcome-only supervision for verifiers — reframes the verification problem.

title: Tree of Thoughts
why: Explicit tree search over CoT branches with self-evaluation — generalizes self-consistency to tree topology.

title: Turpin et al. — CoT can be unfaithful
why: Models often generate post-hoc rationalizations. The visible chain ≠ the computation that produced the answer.

title: DeepSeekMath / GRPO
why: Group Relative Policy Optimization. Cheaper, more stable than PPO for verifiable-reward RL — the workhorse algorithm of the R1 era.

title: Stream of Search
why: Train models to internalize search behavior — pre-R1 evidence that search-like CoT is trainable, not just inferable.

title: AlphaProof — IMO silver
why: Reasoning system reaches IMO silver-medal performance. Theorem-prover-augmented LLM, not pure CoT — but a milestone.

title: Test-time compute scaling laws
who: Snell, Lee, Xu, Kumar — UC Berkeley/Google
why: Crystallizes the regularity: optimally-spent inference compute can outperform parameter scaling on reasoning tasks.

title: OpenAI o1 announcement
why: Long internal CoTs trained via RL with verifiable rewards. Made test-time-compute scaling a product story; the scaling plot became iconic.

title: Tülu 3 — RLVR named
why: First open recipe to formally name and document RL-from-Verifiable-Rewards. Concurrent with R1's research.

title: "Don't think 2+3=?" — Overthinking
why: Reasoning models burn hundreds of tokens on trivial problems and sometimes get them wrong. The first canonical overthinking paper.

title: DeepSeek-R1 / R1-Zero
why: Pure RL from base (no SFT seed) produces o1-class reasoning. Open weights, open recipe — the field's defining release.

title: s1 — Simple Test-Time Scaling
why: Tiny SFT dataset (1k traces) + budget forcing matches o1-preview. Suggests the bar for reasoning is low if the elicitation is right.

title: Claude 3.7 Sonnet — extended thinking
why: First Claude with user-controllable thinking budget. Productionized the test-time-compute knob.

title: Towards Thinking-Optimal Scaling
why: Optimal CoT length is task-dependent and well below the model's default. Framework for choosing the right budget.

title: Reasoning models can also be efficient — open reproductions
why: Independent reproductions of R1 on Qwen-7B, Mistral-7B confirm the recipe is base-model-agnostic and not DeepSeek-specific.

title: Anthropic — Reasoning model faithfulness
why: Re-runs faithfulness probes on Claude with extended thinking; finds reasoning RL only partly fixes the post-hoc-rationalization problem.

title: Don't Overthink it — shorter chains often win
why: At fixed budget, preferring shorter thinking chains beats longer ones on most reasoning benchmarks. Inverse-of-the-default finding.

title: Gemini Deep Think — IMO gold
why: Pure-LLM (no formal solver) reasoning system reaches IMO gold-medal performance.

title: Recursive Self-Aggregation
why: Loop: sample chains → summarize → resample. Trades depth for branching. Often beats single-pass long CoT at fixed budget.

title: ARC-AGI-3 launches
why: New generation-and-search structure designed to resist the R1-era recipe. Where the next round of SOTA chases happen.
